production.note: US model years. Start: GM's May 28, 2013 release is for "The 2014 Corvette Stingray's all-new LT1 6.2L V-8 engine". End: GM's 2019 order guide ("2018 Chevrolet Car (2019) Corvette") still lists the Stingray coupe (1YY07) and convertible (1YY67) with the LT1 (source gm-2019-order-guide), and the 2020 Corvette was the mid-engine C8 (GM: "Chevrolet Introduces First-Ever Mid-Engine Corvette for 2020", source gm-2020-c8-release).

body.note: GM's 2015 specification sheet has columns for the 1YY07 Stingray Coupe and the 1YY67 Stingray Convertible. The coupe is a "2-door hatchback coupe with removable roof panel" (source cac-2014-preliminary-specs). Both bodies were offered from 2014 (2014 order guide lists coupe and convertible model codes, source gm-2014-order-guide).

displacementL.note: 6,162 cc. GM order guide: "Engine, 6.2L (376 ci) V8 DI"; Corvette Action Center's preliminary specification page: "Displacement (cu in / cc): 376 / 6162" (source cac-2014-preliminary-specs).

aspiration.note: No forced induction is mentioned for the LT1; the Z06's supercharged LT4 is a separate record.

fuel.note: Direct-injected gasoline V8 ("Direct injection is a primary contributor to the engine's combustion efficiency").

drivetrain.note: "2-door hatchback coupe with removable roof panel; rear-wheel drive".

transmission.note: 2014: "Transmission, 7-speed manual with Active Rev Matching" or "Transmission, 6-speed paddle shift with automatic mode" (source gm-2014-order-guide). From 2015 the 6-speed automatic was replaced by an eight-speed automatic: 2015 brochure, "7-speed manual transmission with Active Rev Matching" and "available 8-speed paddle-shift automatic transmission"; GM's August 20, 2014 release describes engineering "the new eight-speed automatic to fit the same space as the previous six-speed automatic" (source gm-2015-8speed-release). Both automatics are torque-converter units.

powerHp.note: Standard exhaust. Quote, Chevrolet's 2015 Corvette brochure specifications table, Stingray column: "HORSEPOWER 455 @ 6000 rpm (460 with performance exhaust)"; footnote 1: "455 horsepower with standard engine. 460 horsepower with available dual-mode performance exhaust." Same rating at launch, GM release of May 28, 2013 (source gm-2014-lt1-release): "The Stingray is SAE-certified at 455 horsepower (339 kW) and 460 lb-ft (624 Nm) with the standard exhaust system." and 460 hp with the available performance exhaust. Same rating in GM's 2019 order guide: "Engine, 6.2L (376 ci) V8 DI (455 hp [339.3 kW] @ 6000 rpm, 460 lb-ft of torque [621.0 N-m] @ 4600 rpm)" (source gm-2019-order-guide). The 2014 order guide printed a pre-certification "GM-estimated 450 hp"; the certified figure superseded it.

weightLb.note: Manufacturer curb weight, Stingray coupe, 2015 model year. Quote, GM's 2015 specifications sheet (published May 23, 2014): "Curb weight, lbs. (kg) 3298 (1496) 3362 (1525)" (coupe, convertible). Chevrolet's 2015 brochure prints "Curb weight 3,298 lbs. (coupe) / 3,362 lbs. (convertible)" for both the Stingray and the Stingray with Z51 (source gm-2015-brochure). GM gives one figure per body and does not split it by transmission. For 2014 only an estimate was found (AutoGuide, May 2013: "an estimated curb weight of 3,298 lbs without the Z51 package", not cited as a value), so 2015 is the reference year.
